instruction: You are working in a Go repository checked out at /gin (the gin web framework). Task: a bug was reported in /gin/errors.go. The reported symptom: the test named `TestErrorUnwrap` (in package gin, i.e. `go test -run TestErrorUnwrap ./...`) is expected to pass but does not. The test checks that gin.Error interoperates with errors.Is() and errors.As() per the doc comment on Unwrap() in errors.go. The version of the test that checks this is NOT in the repository, so the test name only describes the expected behaviour; the existing /gin/errors_test.go may be a stale/older version. Investigate /gin/errors.go (and errors_test.go) carefully, determine the real root cause, and fix it by editing /gin/errors.go only (do NOT edit any test file, do NOT add new features). A very likely culprit: method receiver/value-vs-pointer mismatch between `func (msg Error) Error() string` and `func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error`, which breaks errors.Is/errors.As when a gin.Error VALUE (not pointer) is wrapped. Make the fix so that BOTH `&Error{...}` and `Error{...}` (value) wrapped in fmt.Errorf("%w") work with errors.Is and errors.As, and so that `var _ error = &Error{}` still holds. Then verify: (1) `cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./errors.go`; (2) `cd /gin && go test -run TestErrorUnwrap -v .`; (3) write a TEMPORARY throwaway test file in /tmp (e.g. a small main program or a test in a temp dir that imports the local gin via a go.mod replace directive) that checks errors.Is/errors.As work for both a value `Error{Err: innerErr}` and a pointer `&Error{Err: innerErr}` wrapped with fmt.Errorf("%w"), then DELETE that temporary file/dir afterwards so the repository is left clean (git status must show only errors.go modified). Report back: the exact root cause, the exact diff you applied, the commands you ran and their output, and confirmation that `git status --porcelain` in /gin shows only errors.go as modified.

Independent verification task in the Go repo at /gin. Do NOT modify any file except as explicitly allowed below. Steps: (1) run `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` and `cd /gin && git diff` and report them verbatim; confirm the only change is in errors.go. (2) run `cd /gin && go build ./...` and `cd /gin && go test ./...` and report the results (which packages ok/fail). (3) run `cd /gin && go test -run TestErrorUnwrap -v .`. (4) Independently verify the semantic fix: create a throwaway directory /tmp/verify_unwrap with its own go.mod containing `module verify` + `go 1.20` + `require github.com/gin-gonic/gin v0.0.0` + `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`, copy /gin/go.sum if needed, and write a main.go that checks: for both a VALUE `gin.Error{Err: innerErr}` and a POINTER `&gin.Error{Err: innerErr}` wrapped with fmt.Errorf("%w", ...), that errors.Is(err, innerErr) and errors.As(err, &testErr) are true, and that errors.Unwrap returns innerErr. Run `go mod tidy` if needed then `go run .`. Report the exact output. Then DELETE /tmp/verify_unwrap entirely. (5) Report whether the fix is correct and complete, and whether the repo is left clean (git status --porcelain shows only ` M errors.go`).
